excluded: any other Product Hunt rank or vote field
inputs.note: Website fields in the lineup were Product Hunt API redirect URLs, not product domains. X url: queries cannot include '/'; searches used product names, slugs, and listed maker/hunter handles. No Product Hunt pages were loaded.

forecast.name: Gemini 4 Hydrogen
forecast.reason: By far the heaviest X conversation of the day (14,290 in-window posts, still 171 in the first minutes after 00:05 PT) about a new Google model for fast everyday/agentic coding, matching the tagline.

forecast.name: Claude Meetings
forecast.reason: 5,213 in-window posts and an official announcement with 3,580 visible reposts, plus immediate multilingual and news coverage (including a 73k-follower account) as the product is introduced around 00:05 PT.

forecast.name: Expo Simulators
forecast.reason: 648 posts, an official intro with 138 visible reposts, replies from a 9.4M-follower account, and a cluster of mid-size posts about agents testing mobile builds in the cloud — strong developer-community buzz aligned with the tagline.

forecast.name: Google Pixel Tag
forecast.reason: 295 posts of hardware unboxing, review, and availability chatter, including a 527k-follower gadget account (137 likes, 47 reposts) and a 217k-follower Android site; real consumer buzz, but narrower than the two model/feature launches above.

forecast.name: WHOOP Humans
forecast.reason: 35 posts of genuine launch coverage from tech and fitness accounts (largest sampled poster 55k followers) over the prior day, clearly about the new health-data social network, though engagement stays modest.

forecast.name: Paxper
forecast.reason: The only remaining launch with on-topic X posts: a small product-account note that it went live Nov 8 (5 likes, 1 repost). Thin signal, but it is actual buzz, unlike the zero-hit field.

forecast.name: Replicate
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts in the window, but the lineup text is a sharp, free Webflow/Framer-to-Claude/Codex hook and lists a widely followed hunter handle; ranking rests on that text, not observed buzz.

forecast.name: Burnstate
forecast.reason: No on-topic X posts; the tagline (pacing Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor limits in the menu bar) is unusually timely, which is the only reason it sits above other silent launches.

forecast.name: Trainn MCP
forecast.reason: No X posts found; ranked on lineup text alone — an MCP that turns any AI chat into product videos and courses, which is a clear, current-tooling hook.

forecast.name: Pocket Studio for Supabase
forecast.reason: No X posts found; the tagline is a concrete Android Supabase dashboard and SQL editor, a specific gap that is easier to picture than the other silent, more generic tools.
